description: Consumer-repository data for ops/ci_parity/fixtures.py. Each repository names its fixture roots and, per file, the exact rule ids each lane ('semgrep-l9', 'bandit', ...) must report there. A named rule that fires is expected and does not block; a named rule that does not fire is a FAIL; any other finding on a fixture path, and every finding outside the roots, is classified as before. A file under a root with no entry expects nothing, so any finding on it blocks.

Quantum-L9/Enrichment.Inference.Engine.note: CI canary for campaign L9-CI-UNIFIED-LEVERAGE-2026-11-20-v1.7.1 (branch canary/ci-ul-eie). Central semgrep since l9-ci-sdk #134/#139/#143 (pinned by Core #324): tests/ is in required scope, nosemgrep is inert, and a shell=True site is reported once by the L9 rule (the registry duplicate is superseded). So the L9 rule is expected on every shell=True fixture, including the tests/ scope witness and the nosemgrep override attempt. Org-CI cutover canary (branch canary/ci-ul-eie-cutover, EIE cutover Phase 2/3): canary/eie_cutover/ holds the gitleaks word witness and one known-bad file per EIE consumer Semgrep rule; three of them also trip the SDK baseline, named below. The consumer rules are not a ci-parity lane.
